_comment: MEASURED SP-1 Volume resistor-ladder calibration (SAADC AIN1, 12-bit).
Captured on physical hardware with firmware build st20-VOLCAL, transport
STOPPED, via the ST_VOL_CAL capture in main.c's control loop. This file is
the AUTHORITATIVE provenance for decode_vol()'s band edges in src/main.c.
This rail is the companion to docs/ladder-measured.json, which records AIN0
(Track + PLAY). AIN0 was captured in the st16-cal build long ago; AIN1 had
NEVER been measured, and every band edge in decode_vol() was inherited
guesswork. That is what this capture ends -- for the three buttons it
actually exercised.
'lo'/'hi' are the extreme SETTLED values observed for that state: a reading
held within +/-8 counts for 6 consecutive 8 ms control passes, so an edge
sample caught mid-press cannot appear here. 'centre' is the midpoint of
that observed span.
WHAT THIS CAPTURE PROVES. Volume+ (1821..1830) and the two-button chord
(2019..2029) are cleanly separated by 189 counts of empty rail. Before this
measurement decode_vol()'s top band was 'anything >= 1500', so BOTH states
returned VOL_UP and the FX entry chord was undecodable. That was the single
blocker on FX mode, and these numbers remove it.
The chord reading HIGHER than either single press confirms the parallel-
resistor model docs/ladder-measured.json established for AIN0, on this rail
and on real hardware.
IMPORTANT LIMITATION, stated here rather than hidden: FWD and RWD share
this rail and were NEVER PRESSED during the capture. decode_vol()'s two
tempo bands (~404 and ~1220) are therefore still the inherited, unverified
values they always were. They do not conflict with anything measured here
-- no observed plateau falls inside either -- but they are not proven, and
this file does not pretend otherwise. Measuring them needs another
st20-VOLCAL session with those two buttons pressed.
Second limitation, same one AIN0 carries: captured with the transport
STOPPED. Band centres are resistor ratios and do not move with playback;
the JITTER figure is a stopped-state figure.

capture.settle_rule: raw held within +/-8 counts for 6 consecutive 8 ms passes

states.name: volume_chord
states._comment: The FX overlay entry chord. FUNCTION held first selects GLOBAL scope.

_comment: The edges decode_vol() actually uses, and where each came from.
ST_VOL_CHORD_MIN is the one edge this capture placed: the MIDPOINT of the
measured 1830..2019 gap, which sits 95 counts clear of both neighbours.
Symmetric by construction, so noise in either direction has equal room.
Not a centre-plus-tolerance band like st_ladder.c builds for AIN0: this is
the top of the rail, nothing exists above the chord to collide with, so
one threshold is the entire decision.
